prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in League City, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1058; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in League City, Texas, turning left onto the main road.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I had my turn signal on and I was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. I thought the lane was clear, so I started to turn.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began the turn?
A: Not clearly. I looked, but the sun was low and I didn't notice anything coming until it was almost on me.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other car came through from the opposite direction and hit the front passenger side of my vehicle. My head hit the window pretty hard.
Q: Did you lose consciousness or feel dazed afterward?
A: I didn't pass out, but I was confused for a while. I had a headache and was seeing spots, and I couldn't remember exactly what I'd been doing.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: Yes, an ambulance took me to the emergency room. They diagnosed me with a concussion and told me to rest and avoid screens for a while.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. The headaches come and go, and I get tired quickly. My doctor has me off work for now.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?
A: Only that I was following the traffic rules as best I could. I'd like the claim handled as quickly as possible, since I'm still recovering.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
